narrative.title: Issuing Even-Prime License Plates
narrative.scenario: A motor registry issues plate strings where every even position must carry an even digit and every odd position must carry one of the four single-digit primes. With five even digits and four primes available, each slot's freedom multiplies, and the registry needs the count of valid plates of any requested length modulo 10^9 + 7. The count grows by a factor of 5 per even slot and 4 per odd slot.
narrative.inputFormat: A single integer n, the plate length.
narrative.outputFormat: The number of valid digit strings of length n, modulo 10^9 + 7.

complexity.optimalTime: O(log n) with fast exponentiation (the source uses O(n))
complexity.optimalSpace: O(n) recursion stack in the source form

testCases.explanation: One slot, which is even-indexed: any of the five even digits.
Two even slots and two prime slots: 5 * 4 * 5 * 4 = 400.

hintLevels: Level 1: Slots are independent — the total is a product of per-slot choice counts, not a search.
Level 2: Even-indexed slots (0, 2, 4, ...) allow 5 digits; odd-indexed allow 4. Ceiling(n/2) even slots and floor(n/2) odd slots.
Level 3: n reaches 10^15, so linear multiplication overflows both time and patience — raise 5 and 4 to their slot counts with modular fast exponentiation.
